summary: Caribou Point light at the north end of Caribou Island, first lit 1868; its towers were rebuilt in 1916 and about 1970, it was destaffed in 1990, and it still shows.

notes_for_editor: (1) Second tower year: Lighthouse Friends gives 1915 (contract to W. Talbot of Pictou for $5,103.11); the Society and the tourism guide give 1916; the Marine report for fiscal 1915-16 lists the erection and names W. Talbot against it. The Talbot match was checked on the page image (scan p. 52, printed p. 45) on 2026-10-28: the Caribou row reads 'Erection of a wooden combined lighthouse tower and dwelling', 'Contract', 'W. Talbot, Pictou, N.S.', with 2,650.00 expended in fiscal 1915-16. Not resolved; the story gives both, and says the sources do not show when the rest of the contract price was paid. (2) Third tower: Lighthouse Friends says about 1971; the Society and the tourism guide say 1968 to 1970. Not resolved. (3) Keeper Munroe: the list spells the name Munore, the text Munroe; the roster uses Munroe. (4) Keeper D. Falconer was checked on the page image (1911 report, scan p. 242, printed p. 235): the row reads Caribou Island, D. Falconer. The 1912 day-beacon line for Caribou channel was dropped from the story: it concerns the channel, not this light, and it had only been matched by column position. (5) Island: Lighthouse Friends puts the point on the north end of Caribou Island; the Coast Guard list on Gull Point at the NE end of Caribou Island; the Society on Caribou Point at the NE end of Gull Island. The story states all three. Same-name traps avoided: the Marine reports list other Caribou Islands (Lake Superior and Ontario light lists, and a 1923 loss 'off Caribou island in a severe storm' that belongs to the Lake Superior island), a 'River Caribou' in Quebec, and a 'Caribou island, N.S.' row in a 1920 list of pole lights that has no clear station match. None is used. (6) Gap: no keeper is named between 1966 and 1971 in any source read. (7) Private residence: Lighthouse Friends names the owners of the second tower's house; the story does not name them. (8) Keepers who served after about 1960 (Richards, Welsh) are named only in their public role, with no detail beyond what Lighthouse Friends prints. (9) Not read: the Chance Heritage Trust page (appears in search results only), the Facebook group and the Flickr captions. Newspapers not searched (Canadian station; Chronicling America is US). (10) Corrections: none proposed. The record's first_lit (1868), the position and the Coast Guard characteristic agree. (11) Access: by car to the end of Caribou Island Road; grounds open, tower closed; Coast Guard property. (12) Photos: none added.
